## The Right Object (eigenvector L^2, not trace mass)

The gap is a property of the top eigenpair `(lambda_i, v_i)` of
`T_beta = E D_beta E`, `E = exp((beta/2)J)`, `D_beta = diag r_(p,q)`. Piece (3)
must bound how much of the gap operator's spectral content lives at weights
OUTSIDE the active window, i.e. the `L^2` mass of the EIGENVECTORS `v_0` (Perron)
and `v_1` (first-excited) outside the window.

This is NOT the dimension-weighted trace mass `sum_{p,q} dim(p,q) r_(p,q)`: that
object is FAT (the degree-6 dimension factor `dim ~ pq(p+q)/2` pushes its mass to
moderate `Q`; the runner shows `>= 7%` of it sits beyond `Q > 2.5^2` and the
fraction grows with `beta`). The `L^2`-normalized eigenvectors, by contrast,
concentrate at the saddle and decay there — they are the correct tail object.

## The Window and the Support Calculation

With `a = (p,q)/sqrt(beta)`, the natural window is the A2 Casimir/saddle level set

```text
Q(a) = (p^2 + p q + q^2)/beta = 3 C2(p,q)/beta   (leading),
```

`Q = x^2 + x y + y^2` the A2 quadratic form. The diagonal is saddle-suppressed,
`r_(p,q) ~ beta^(3/2) H(a) exp(-Q(a))` (rung six). The support calculation tests
the expected reading that the top eigenvectors of `E D_beta E` inherit a
polynomial times Gaussian suppression in `Q`,

```text
|v_i(p,q)|^2  <=  (poly) exp(-kappa Q(a)),   kappa >= 1,
```

with an `O(1)` rate `kappa`. The runner witnesses deep-tail rates
`kappa ~ 1.2-1.6` on the tested grid, faster than `1`, so the finite-grid evidence
is consistent with the desired outside-weight upper-bound direction. This note
does not prove the analytic inheritance step for all beta.

```text
sum_{Q(a) > A^2} |v_i(p,q)|^2  <=  eps_i(A),   eps_i(A) small on the tested grid.
```

## Witnessed Finite-Grid Tail (not fitted)

The runner builds `T_beta`, diagonalizes, and computes the eigenvector `L^2`
tails across `beta in {48,108,192,300}`:

| beta | v0 (Q>2.5^2) | v0 (Q>3^2) | v0 (Q>3.5^2) | v1 (Q>2.5^2) | v1 (Q>3^2) | v1 (Q>3.5^2) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 48 | 9.0e-3 | 2.7e-4 | 3.4e-6 | 1.05e-1 | 7.1e-3 | 1.7e-4 |
| 108 | 1.4e-2 | 5.0e-4 | 6.3e-6 | 1.41e-1 | 1.2e-2 | 2.9e-4 |
| 192 | 1.7e-2 | 6.7e-4 | 9.1e-6 | 1.64e-1 | 1.5e-2 | 4.0e-4 |
| 300 | 1.9e-2 | 7.8e-4 | 1.1e-5 | 1.77e-1 | 1.7e-2 | 4.7e-4 |

Four finite-grid facts are witnessed:

1. Smallness at the `A = 3.5` window: `v_0` tail `<= 1.1e-5`, `v_1` tail
   `<= 4.7e-4`, across the tested `beta` grid.
2. SUPER-GAUSSIAN decay in `A`: each `+0.5` in `A` divides the tail by `>= 25`
   (`v_0`), confirming the Gaussian cutoff in `Q`.
3. The `beta`-creep at fixed `A` is decreasing on this grid: the `v_1`(A=3)
   increments shrink `4.6e-3 -> 3.2e-3 -> 2.0e-3`. This is evidence for bounded
   behavior, not a proof of convergence for all beta.
4. `v_1` is `~22-26x` FATTER than `v_0` (`v_1` is the first-excited, even
   `p<->q` mode and spreads more; it is one-signed along the diagonal ray) — but
   still uniformly suppressed.

The constant is poly-modulated (the effective rate rises with `A`, the signature
of a polynomial times a Gaussian), so this is not a single `exp(-c A^2)` rate. The
load-bearing output here is bounded support: the correct `L^2` object and exact
finite-grid tail values, with the `A ~ 3.5` window giving `<= ~5e-4` on the tested
grid.

## Anti-Fabrication

The tails are computed from the exact finite matrices (`np.linalg.eigh` of the
operator), normalized; no `curve_fit`/`polyfit`, no target value, no closure
constant. The window `Q = (p^2+pq+q^2)/beta` is the A2 Casimir form; the measured
deep-tail `kappa ~ 1.2-1.6` supports, but does not prove, the desired
`(poly) exp(-kappa Q)` density bound. The dimension-weighted contrast identifies
the correct tail object (the eigenvector `L^2`, not the fat trace mass).

## Falsifiers

- The dimension-weighted trace mass tail is FAT (`>= 7%` beyond `Q > 2.5^2`,
  growing with `beta`) — the wrong tail object; using it would give no uniform
  domination. The eigenvector `L^2` tail is the right object.
- A fixed window (not `Q`/`sqrt(beta)`-scaled) would not give uniformity (cf.
  W92's mode-tail analogue).

## Honest Outcome

This note supplies bounded support for H_det ingredient (3): the gap eigenvectors'
`L^2` mass beyond the `Q(a) > A^2` window is small on the tested grid
(`eps_{v0}(3.5) ~ 1e-5`, `eps_{v1}(3.5) ~ 5e-4`) and uses the right object for the
outside-weight tail. It does not derive the beta-uniform analytic tail theorem.
The missing work is a proof of the eigenvector-density bound or a sparse/scaled
extension that turns the finite-grid witness into a theorem. The `K_W(A)` assembly
and H_spec remain open; H_det and the half-line gap theorem are NOT closed by this
note.
